## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin, and gaunt woman with sharp angles and no curves, who was a dark, homely child. Her dark hair, which shows gray streaks, is worn twisted up in a hard little knot at the back with two wire hairpins stuck aggressively through it. Though her face has softened over time, her hair has grown grayer and she can look old, worn, and tired.

## Personality

A woman of narrow experience, Marilla Cuthbert is defined by her rigid conscience, self-contained nature, and sensible, sober demeanor. She exhibits a strict and critical disposition, often stoic and unromantic, though she can occasionally display a sarcastic streak. Deeply repressed, she considers displays of deep emotion unseemly, rarely showing excitement and maintaining a customary calm. Her motivation has centered on drilling [Anne](../character/anne.md) into a tranquil uniformity of disposition, though she also held a secret hope for [Anne](../character/anne.md) to marry [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), a prospect that brings her immense happiness. In addition to her strict character, she is known for making three-year-old homemade currant wine and crafting round braided mats. While she detests cats and is prone to headaches, she nonetheless worries significantly about [Anne](../character/anne.md).

## History

Marilla Cuthbert grew up as a dark, homely child and spent a cramped childhood at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), where she obeyed orders and remained sensitive about her early looks for fifty years. In her youth, she quarreled out of willful pride with John [Blythe](../character/blythe.md), refused to forgive him when he asked, and rejected him, leading to blighted hopes and hidden dreams that she carried through sixty years of living at the house. Having inherited an amethyst brooch from her mother and lived peacefully alongside her neighbor [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) for forty-five years, Marilla's quiet routine was altered when she and her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) set out to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, only to receive a young girl named [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) instead. Though initially shocked and intent on returning [Anne](../character/anne.md), Marilla was moved to pity after hearing the child's tragic background and agreed to let her stay. As she undertook the task of raising, educating, and disciplining the imaginative girl, Marilla developed a deep love and warmth for [Anne](../character/anne.md), realizing the true extent of her affection when [Anne](../character/anne.md) broke her ankle in an accident. Over the passing years, Marilla guided [Anne](../character/anne.md) through her school days, managed her home when she took in the orphaned Keith twins after her cousin Mary's death, and opened her house to [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) after [Rachel](../character/rachel-lynde.md) was widowed. When failing eyesight threatened to force the sale of [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) after Matthew's sudden death, Marilla was spared from losing her home when [Anne](../character/anne.md) gave up a college scholarship to stay, teach locally, and live beside her. Marilla later cheered Anne's eventual entry into [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), comforted her through her heartbreak over [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) Blythe's near-fatal illness, and happily helped prepare for Anne's marriage to [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) in the [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) orchard. In her later years, Marilla traveled to [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor) to visit [Anne](../character/anne.md), remaining a steadfast source of comfort through the heartbreaking loss of Anne's firstborn daughter and returning later to celebrate the birth of her healthy grandson, [James Matthew](../character/james-a.md).

## Quotes

> "Well now, yes. It always kind of gives me a thrill to see them ugly white grubs that spade up in the cucumber beds. I hate the look of them."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P58](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0058)

> "It’s five miles; and as you’re evidently bent on talking you might as well talk to some purpose by telling me what you know about yourself."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P8](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0008)

> "No, I don’t want any of your imaginings. Just you stick to bald facts. Begin at the beginning. Where were you born and how old are you?"
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P10](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0010)

> "We’re not talking about poetry, Anne—we are talking about saying your prayers. Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P11](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0011)

> "Well, you’ll have to do without your thrill. I hadn’t any material to waste on puffed sleeves. I think they are ridiculous-looking things anyhow. I prefer the plain, sensible ones."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XI. Anne’s Impressions of Sunday-school P10](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0010)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla initially took in [Anne](../character/anne.md) by mistake, intending to adopt a boy to help on the farm, but decided to keep her after learning of her difficult past as an orphan. As her primary guardian and mentor, Marilla acts as a strict figure who enforces discipline, orders [Anne](../character/anne.md) to her room for outbursts, and teaches her practical life skills like cooking and prayers. Over time, Marilla grows deeply affectionate toward [Anne](../character/anne.md), coming to love her as her adoptive daughter while managing Anne's intense imagination and fiery temper.

- Commands — guardian ordering her to her room  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P22](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0022), [v2 XII A Jonah Day P35](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0035)</sub>

Though Mrs. Lynde's outspoken criticisms of [Anne](../character/anne.md) occasionally cause friction, Marilla turns to her for guidance on raising the girl, and the two maintain a reliable, comforting bond during times of difficulty.
